messages.text: make this repo easier for coding agents to work in
I’ll inspect the repo’s structure and development workflow, then add guidance and checks that help coding agents make and verify changes.

This is a small, dependency-free Node CLI. The main gaps are undocumented input/output rules and no tests for command-line behavior. I’ll add a root `AGENTS.md`, expand the README, and test the CLI’s output and failure cases.

Node 24 is available here; npm and Git metadata are absent, so I’ll verify with direct Node commands.

The guidance now covers the source map, stock rules, CSV format, and verification commands. I’ve also added CLI tests for report generation, paths with spaces, exit codes, and preserving an existing report when input fails.

The original five tests pass. This sandbox needs a command-scoped OpenSSL override to start Node’s test runner; I’ve documented that workaround and am checking the expanded suite.

Added:

- [AGENTS.md](arms/without-um/repo/AGENTS.md) with a source map, verification commands, and compatibility constraints.
- Expanded README with setup, input/output rules, examples, and exit codes.
- Nine CLI regression tests covering report generation, error handling, and preserving existing reports on invalid input.

All **14 tests pass** using `OPENSSL_CONF=/dev/null node --test`. The README example and documentation links also check out.

This is a small, dependency-free Node CLI. The main gaps are a sparse README, no agent instructions, and no tests for the command-line workflow. I’ll document the input/output contract, add a focused `AGENTS.md`, and cover the CLI’s success and failure paths.

This checkout has no Git metadata, and npm is unavailable here. Node is available, so I can run the checks directly without installing anything.

The agent guide and expanded README are in place. They cover where to make changes, compatibility requirements, and commands for focused tests. The new CLI tests cover report generation, exit codes, file errors, and preserving an existing report when input is invalid.

The original five tests pass. This sandbox blocks Node’s system OpenSSL configuration file, so I’m using `OPENSSL_CONF=/dev/null` for verification.
